name: School Ready
tagline: Confident on day one of school, no flashcards
about: School Ready prepares 3–5-year-olds for nursery, preschool or their first year of school: the skills that actually matter (self-care, listening, turn-taking, early letters and numbers), a countdown plan, separation-anxiety scripts and a first-week routine for the whole family.
persona: You are an early-years teacher who has welcomed hundreds of new starters: calm, practical, and clear that independence and confidence beat academics at this age.

onboarding.title: Ready for the big day
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us the start date and what they can do already.
bullets: Countdown plan to the first day

tools.title: Readiness check
tools.subtitle: What matters, what doesn't
tools.prompt: Create a school-readiness check for the profile child, start date and setting. Sections: a checklist grouped by area (self-care, communication, social, listening and attention, physical, early literacy and maths) with what 'ready enough' means for each, a table (Skill | Practise by | Playful way to practise | Fine if not yet), bullets on what schools genuinely do not expect, and a callout addressing the profile's biggest worry.

tools.title: Countdown plan
tools.subtitle: Weeks left → weekly focus

inputs.label: Skills to work on
inputs.placeholder: zips, sitting for a story, name recognition

tools.prompt: Build a {weeks}-week countdown plan for the profile child focusing on: {gaps}. Sections: a table (Week | Focus skill | Daily 5-minute game | Weekend outing or visit), steps for the final week (uniform tries, route walk, earlier bedtimes), a checklist of things to buy or label, and a callout on visiting the setting and meeting the teacher.

tools.title: Goodbye script
tools.subtitle: Drop-offs without the drama
tools.prompt: Write a drop-off plan for '{stage}' matched to the profile child's temperament. Sections: a quote with the exact goodbye script (short, same words each day) and what NOT to say, steps for the drop-off routine from door to classroom, bullets on what the teacher will do after you leave and how to ask for updates, and a callout on when clinginess suggests something to look into.

tools.title: Teach a school skill
tools.subtitle: One independence skill, playfully

inputs.label: Skill
options: Opening lunch and eating in 20 min

tools.prompt: Teach '{skill}' to the profile child in {days} days. Sections: steps broken into the smallest teachable parts with a rhyme or cue for each, a table (Day | Practice moment | Parent does | Child does), bullets on common blockers for the profile temperament, and a quote with the praise line that names the effort.

tools.title: First-week survival
tools.subtitle: Routine, meals, meltdowns
tools.prompt: Design a first-week routine for the profile family given: {hours} and {notes}. Sections: a table (Time | Weekday routine | Who does what), a checklist for the night-before bag and the morning, bullets on after-school restraint collapse (snacks, quiet, no questions yet), and a callout on the profile's biggest worry with a fallback plan.

disclaimer: General guidance, not a developmental assessment. If you're concerned about your child's development, talk to your health visitor, paediatrician or the setting's SENCO.
